attribution.note: Marcus writes in his own voice, in his own post, describing what the paper shows. It is his characterisation of the paper, not a quote from someone else.

semantics.note: The normalised proposition keeps his framing: the paper and its taxonomy show the result, and 'in many ways' is kept. It is a firm present-tense observation about a publication.

contract.note: Marcus gave no measure. Reading 'shows' as the taxonomy's qualitative comparison is fair and ordinary, because his sentence points to the taxonomy. The contract correctly says there is no matched stateless control.

evidence.note: This is the linked preprint, dated 2026-02-20, before the post. Section 3.2 says its six vulnerability classes are unique to agents or significantly amplified in them compared with stateless LLMs. That matches the support condition.

reviews.rationale: The cited paper's taxonomy sets out six classes of agent vulnerability and says each is unique to agents or significantly amplified compared with stateless LLMs. It explains them through agent parts such as memory, tools and delegation. That meets the support condition on the plain qualitative reading. The paper has no controlled numerical comparison against stateless models, but the claim, as worded and contracted, does not need one. No counterevidence was found.
